claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant because aggregate launch readiness passed and the known merchant dispute support gap can be handled through explicit documentation and post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the launch satisfies the disclosure policy threshold.
A material weakness exists if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
If the weakness is material, launch requires either resolution, pre-launch disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate.
evidence_requests: Evidence that the material limitation was formally disclosed in the required pre-launch model card or equivalent launch artifact.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance authorizing launch despite the unresolved named-segment gap.
Final legal determination on whether and how the merchant dispute support gap must be disclosed.
Evidence showing whether the affected segment is a named launch use case, in addition to being tied to contractual renewal commitments.
specific_concerns: The merchant dispute support weakness affects a segment named in two marketplace renewal commitments, which supports materiality under the stated policy.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has been completed before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved gap.
Legal review is still open, which the policy text says prevents product labeling such as non-core from resolving materiality.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record rather than merely arguable.
That aggregate readiness plus monitoring is sufficient without proving disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that the materiality issue is adequately closed for launch certification.
